name: Idesa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, John Muniru, David Onoja, Lewinan Andrew & Samuel Eju. 2024. A Sociolinguistic Profile of Five Southern Northwestern Edoid Languages in Southern Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2024-012. Dallas: SIL International. 72 pp. (Glottolog ref 700271; sole Glottolog's most extensive description for ides1238)
sources.note: Nothing. Only first-hand Idesa/Orake data anywhere: 222-item Orake wordlist (Otuo, 20 Sept 2021) and sec. 8.3 'Phonetic inventories' pp.27-30 (pooled consonant/vowel charts, labialisation/palatalisation). sec. 4 p.6: 'In this report, we refer to Idesa as Orake.. There does not appear to be anything published on Orake.' Appendix F p.48: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no analysis of tones and no in-depth analysis of other phonological or phonetic features.' No occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent'.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages (4th ed.). p.81 'Okpe-Idesa-Akuku'.
sources.note: Classification/identity entry for the cluster; no phonology expected.

sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben Ohi. 1989. Edoid. In J. Bendor-Samuel (ed.), The Niger-Congo Languages, 291-304. Lanham: University Press of America.
sources.note: 'Okpe-Idesa' / 'Okpe-Akuku-Idesa' in the classification list only; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben Ohiomamhe. 1989. Comparative Edoid: Phonology and Lexicon (Delta Series 6). Port Harcourt: University of Port Harcourt Press.
sources.note: Nothing on Idesa. p.10: 'Ghotuo (a NCE language) and the Idesa dialect of Okpe (a NWE language) exist side by side at Otuo'; p.11 ethnohistory (Idesa shifted to NWE Okpe). Classification 1.3.4 'Okpe-Akuku-Idesa'. Ch. 4 phonologies do not cover NWE Okpe/Idesa; sec. 3.5 Tone pp.47-48 family-level only (Edoid = three levels or two levels +/- downstep); the word 'stress' never occurs.
Conflates Idesa with Delta-State Okpe [oke]; no Idesa content, nothing on stress.
